_about: The dwelling side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of God's dwelling and presence that more than one book shares, from the tabernacle and the temple to the psalms, the prophets, the Gospels, the letters and Revelation, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: I will dwell among them

The Law & history: make a sanctuary for Me, so that I may dwell among them
I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God
so that I might dwell among them
so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them
For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites
I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel
We will dwell among you and become one people
Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day
the Canaanites dwell among the Ephraimites to this day
the Canaanites continued to dwell among them in Gezer
The Prophets: where I will dwell among the Israelites forever
I will dwell among them forever
for I am coming to dwell among you
You dwell in the midst of deception
the foreigners who dwell among you
Gospels & Acts: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us

rows.alike: Each speaks of a dwelling "among" a people: "so that I may dwell among them" (Exodus 25:8), "I will dwell among the Israelites" (1 Kings 6:13), "where I will dwell among the Israelites forever" (Ezekiel 43:7), "I am coming to dwell among you" (Zechariah 2:10), and "made His dwelling among us" (John 1:14).
rows.different: In Exodus and Numbers the LORD speaks in the first person, and the dwelling is tied to the sanctuary and the camp: "so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them" (Numbers 5:3). Ezekiel 43:7 has "forever"; Zechariah 2:11 has "many nations will join themselves to the LORD"; John 1:14 is the narrator's sentence, and the one who dwells is "The Word" that "became flesh".

rows.title: Walking among them

The Law & history: the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden
I will walk among you and be your God
the LORD your God walks throughout your camp
I have moved about with a tent as My dwelling
The letters: 2 Corinthians 6:16
I will dwell with them and walk among them
Revelation: walks among the seven golden lampstands

rows.alike: Each speaks of walking among or throughout something: "I will walk among you" (Leviticus 26:12), "walks throughout your camp" (Deuteronomy 23:14), "walk among them" (2 Corinthians 6:16), and "walks among the seven golden lampstands" (Revelation 2:1).
rows.different: Genesis 3:8 is what the man and his wife heard: "the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden". In 2 Samuel 7:6 it is set against a house: "I have not dwelt in a house" but "moved about with a tent as My dwelling". Deuteronomy 23:14 goes on "Your camp must be holy"; 2 Corinthians 6:16 introduces it with "As God has said"; Revelation 2:1 gives it as "the words of Him who holds the seven stars in His right hand".

rows.title: Called a temple: “in three days I will raise it up”, “the temple of His body”, “your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit”

Gospels & Acts: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again
This temple took forty-six years to build
Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body
After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this
I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days
You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days
You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days
The letters: 1 Corinthians 3:16
you yourselves are God's temple, and that God's Spirit dwells in you
1 Corinthians 3:17
God's temple is holy, and you are that temple
1 Corinthians 6:19
your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you
2 Corinthians 6:16
For we are the temple of the living God
Ephesians 2:21
the whole building is fitted together and grows into a holy temple in the Lord
Revelation: I saw no temple in the city, because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple

rows.alike: Each verse says in its own words what it calls a temple: "the temple of His body" (John 2:21), "you yourselves are God's temple" (1 Corinthians 3:16), "your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit" (1 Corinthians 6:19), "we are the temple of the living God" (2 Corinthians 6:16), "the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple" (Revelation 21:22).
rows.different: John 2:21 is the narrator's comment on Jesus' words "Destroy this temple", to which the Jews answer "This temple took forty-six years to build", and John 2:22 goes on "After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this". Matthew 26:61 has others saying of Him "I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days", and Matthew 27:40 and Mark 15:29 have "destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days" said to Him. The letters speak to their readers as "you" and "we", of "your body" in 1 Corinthians 6:19 and of "the whole building" in Ephesians 2:21. Revelation 21:22 has "I saw no temple in the city".

rows.title: The cloud filled the house, and the glory of the LORD filled it

The Law & history: there in a cloud the glory of the LORD appeared
the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle
Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle
the cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD appeared
the cloud filled the house of the LORD
the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud. For the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD
the temple, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud
For the glory of the LORD filled the house of God
fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple
The priests were unable to enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD had filled it
Psalms & wisdom: the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides
The Prophets: a cloud filled the inner court
The temple was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the LORD
the glory of the LORD filled the temple
the glory of the LORD filling His temple
I will fill this house with glory
the train of His robe filled the temple

rows.alike: The same words recur for the tent and the house: "the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle" (Exodus 40:34), "the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD" (1 Kings 8:11), "the glory of the LORD filled the temple" (2 Chronicles 7:1; Ezekiel 43:5), with the cloud beside it in Exodus, Kings, Chronicles and Ezekiel 10:4.
rows.different: At the tent "Moses was unable to enter"; at the temple "the priests could not stand there to minister", and Chronicles adds that "fire came down from heaven". Ezekiel 43:5 is in the first person ("the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court"); Haggai 2:7 is the LORD's promise, "I will fill this house with glory"; Psalm 26:8 speaks of "the place where Your glory resides".

rows.title: The glory departed, and the glory entered

The Law & history: The glory has departed from Israel
The glory has departed from Israel
The Prophets: the glory of the LORD moved away from the threshold of the temple
they stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD, with the glory of the God of Israel above them
the glory of the LORD rose up from within the city and stood over the mountain east of the city
the glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east

rows.alike: Both speak of the glory going from where it had been: "The glory has departed from Israel" (1 Samuel 4:21) and "the glory of the LORD moved away from the threshold of the temple" (Ezekiel 10:18).
rows.different: In 1 Samuel the words are a mother's as she named her son Ichabod, "because the ark of God had been captured". In Ezekiel it is told of the glory itself: it "stood over the mountain east of the city" (11:23), and in 43:4 "entered the temple through the gate facing east".

rows.title: A pillar of cloud by day, a pillar of fire by night

The Law & history: in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day, and in a pillar of fire to give them light by night
Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place before the people
The pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them
the LORD looked down on the army of the Egyptians from the pillar of fire and cloud
the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent
the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night
the cloud would cover the tabernacle by day, and at night it would appear like fire
You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night
in the fire by night and in the cloud by day
the LORD appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud
You led them with a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night
By day the pillar of cloud never turned away from guiding them on their path; and by the night the pillar of fire illuminated the way they should go
Psalms & wisdom: He led them with a cloud by day and with a light of fire all night
He spread a cloud as a covering and a fire to light up the night
The Prophets: a cloud of smoke by day and a glowing flame of fire by night
The letters: 1 Corinthians 10:1
our forefathers were all under the cloud

rows.alike: Cloud by day and fire by night are paired again and again: "a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night" (Numbers 14:14; Nehemiah 9:12), "He led them with a cloud by day" (Psalm 78:14), "a cloud of smoke by day and a glowing flame of fire by night" (Isaiah 4:5).
rows.different: Exodus, Numbers and Deuteronomy tell of the journey from Egypt; Nehemiah 9 addresses God ("You led them"); Isaiah 4:5 speaks of what "the LORD will create over all of Mount Zion"; 1 Corinthians 10:1 says "our forefathers were all under the cloud" and goes on "they all passed through the sea".

rows.title: A voice from the cloud

The Law & history: I will come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you
the LORD called to Moses from within the cloud
the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses
the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance to the Tent, and summoned Aaron and Miriam
out of the fire, the cloud, and the deep darkness on the mountain
Psalms & wisdom: I answered you from the cloud of thunder
He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud
Gospels & Acts: a bright cloud enveloped them, and a voice from the cloud said
a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and a voice came from the cloud
they were afraid as they entered the cloud
a voice came from the cloud

rows.alike: Speech out of a cloud is told: "the LORD called to Moses from within the cloud" (Exodus 24:16), "He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud" (Psalm 99:7), and "a voice came from the cloud" (Mark 9:7; Luke 9:35).
rows.different: At Sinai and the tent the voice gives commandments and summons: "The LORD spoke these commandments in a loud voice" (Deuteronomy 5:22). In the Gospels the voice says "This is My beloved Son" (Matthew 17:5; Mark 9:7) or "This is My Son, whom I have chosen" (Luke 9:35), and adds "Listen to Him!"

rows.title: A dwelling for His Name

The Law & history: the place the LORD your God will choose from among all your tribes to establish as a dwelling for His Name
the LORD your God will choose a dwelling for His Name
the place where the LORD your God chooses to put His Name
at the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name
the place where the LORD your God will choose to put His Name
in the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for His Name
at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for His Name
in the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name
go to the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for His Name
the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name
I have chosen Jerusalem for My Name to be there
the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name
May God, who has caused His Name to dwell there
the place I have chosen as a dwelling for My Name
Psalms & wisdom: they have defiled the dwelling place of Your Name
The Prophets: the place in Shiloh where I first made a dwelling for My Name

rows.alike: The words "a dwelling for His Name" recur through Deuteronomy, each time with the LORD choosing it ("will choose"); Nehemiah 1:9 has "the place I have chosen as a dwelling for My Name", Psalm 74:7 "the dwelling place of Your Name", and Jeremiah 7:12 "where I first made a dwelling for My Name".
rows.different: Deuteronomy speaks of a place the LORD "will choose" without naming it; Chronicles names it: "I have chosen Jerusalem for My Name to be there" (2 Chronicles 6:6). Psalm 74:7 says "they have defiled" it; Jeremiah 7:12 names Shiloh: "see what I did to it".

rows.title: A house for My Name; the house that bears My Name

The Law & history: He will build a house for My Name
a house for the Name of the LORD had not yet been built
he could not build a house for the Name of the LORD his God
I plan to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God
to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel
Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well
your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name
I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel
this house I have built is called by Your Name
by putting My Name there forever; My eyes and My heart will be there for all time
I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name
In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish My Name forever
it was in my heart to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God
You are not to build a house for My Name because you have shed so much blood
He is the one who will build a house for My Name
the temple that will be built for the Name of the LORD
You are not to build a house for My Name, because you are a man of war
Solomon purposed to build a house for the Name of the LORD
I am about to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God
to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel
Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well
your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name
I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel
the place where You said You would put Your Name
this house I have built is called by Your Name
I have now chosen and consecrated this temple so that My Name may be there forever. My eyes and My heart will be there for all time
I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name
for Your Name is in this temple
In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish My Name forever
The Prophets: stand before Me in this house, which bears My Name
what I did to Shiloh I will now do to the house that bears My Name
They have set up their abominations in the house that bears My Name
I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears My Name
They have placed their abominations in the house that bears My Name
You made a covenant before Me in the house that bears My Name

rows.alike: In Samuel, Kings and Chronicles the temple is "a house for My Name", of which the LORD said "My Name shall be there" (1 Kings 8:29) and which is "called by Your Name" (1 Kings 8:43); in Jeremiah it is "this house, which bears My Name" (7:10).
rows.different: In the histories the words belong to the promise to David and to Solomon's building and prayer, with "My eyes and My heart will be there for all time" (1 Kings 9:3), and the warning "I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name" (1 Kings 9:7). In Jeremiah they come with charges, "They have set up their abominations in the house that bears My Name" (7:30), and with "what I did to Shiloh I will now do to the house that bears My Name" (7:14).

rows.title: Shiloh, and what was done to it

The Law & history: the whole congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting there
the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh
she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh
the LORD continued to appear at Shiloh
Psalms & wisdom: He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men
The Prophets: go now to the place in Shiloh where I first made a dwelling for My Name, and see what I did to it
what I did to Shiloh I will now do to the house that bears My Name
I will make this house like Shiloh
this house will become like Shiloh and this city will be desolate and deserted

rows.alike: Shiloh is named as the place of the tent or house: "set up the Tent of Meeting there" (Joshua 18:1), "the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men" (Psalm 78:60), "where I first made a dwelling for My Name" (Jeremiah 7:12).
rows.different: The histories tell of the tent set up and that "the LORD continued to appear at Shiloh"; Psalm 78:60 says "He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh"; Jeremiah sets it beside "this house": "I will make this house like Shiloh" (26:6), words for which the people "assembled against Jeremiah" (26:9).

rows.title: Will God dwell on earth? Not in houses made by hands

The Law & history: But will God indeed dwell upon the earth? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built
But will God indeed dwell with man upon the earth?
man-made gods of wood and stone
Gospels & Acts: I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands
the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands
does not live in temples made by human hands
man-made gods are no gods at all
The letters: 2 Corinthians 5:1
a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands
Hebrews 8:2
the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man
Hebrews 9:11
the greater and more perfect tabernacle that is not made by hands
Hebrews 9:24
Christ did not enter a man-made copy of the true sanctuary, but He entered heaven itself

rows.alike: Solomon asks "will God indeed dwell upon the earth?" and says "much less this temple I have built" (1 Kings 8:27); Acts has "the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands" (7:48) and "does not live in temples made by human hands" (17:24); Hebrews speaks of a tabernacle "not made by hands" (9:11).
rows.different: Solomon says it in the prayer at the temple he built. Mark 14:58 is what is reported as heard from Jesus ("We heard Him say"), setting "this man-made temple" against "another that is made without hands". Stephen (Acts 7:48) and Paul (Acts 17:24) say it to their hearers; Hebrews sets "a man-made copy" against "the true sanctuary" (9:24); 2 Corinthians 5:1 sets "the earthly tent we live in" against "an eternal house in heaven". Daniel 2:34 has the words "not by human hands" of "a stone".

rows.title: Zeal for Your house

Psalms & wisdom: zeal for Your house has consumed me
Gospels & Acts: Zeal for Your house will consume Me

rows.alike: Both say "Zeal for Your house" and that it consumes the speaker.
rows.different: Psalm 69:9 says "has consumed me" and goes on "the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me". In John 2:17 it is what "His disciples remembered", with "it is written" and "will consume Me".

rows.title: The LORD is in His holy temple

The Law & history: from His temple He heard my voice
Psalms & wisdom: in reverence I will bow down toward Your holy temple
The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD is on His heavenly throne
From His temple He heard my voice
when I lift up my hands toward Your holy sanctuary
they have defiled Your holy temple
I bow down toward Your holy temple
The Prophets: yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple
My prayer went up to You, to Your holy temple
the Lord from His holy temple
But the LORD is in His holy temple; let all the earth be silent before Him

rows.alike: "The LORD is in His holy temple" stands in Psalm 11:4 and Habakkuk 2:20; prayer turns "toward Your holy temple" in Psalms 5:7 and 138:2 and in Jonah 2:4; and "from His temple He heard my voice" is in both 2 Samuel 22:7 and Psalm 18:6.
rows.different: Psalm 11:4 pairs it with "the LORD is on His heavenly throne", Habakkuk 2:20 with "let all the earth be silent before Him", and Micah 1:2 with "May the Lord GOD bear witness against you". Jonah prays it having said "I have been banished from Your sight" (2:4); Psalm 79:1 says the nations "have defiled Your holy temple".

rows.title: A voice from the temple

The Prophets: listen to the voice from the temple! It is the voice of the LORD
Revelation: another angel came out of the temple, crying out in a loud voice
I heard a loud voice from the temple
a loud voice came from the throne in the temple

rows.alike: Isaiah 66:6 has "the voice from the temple" and Revelation 16:1 "a loud voice from the temple", and 16:17 "a loud voice came from the throne in the temple".
rows.different: Isaiah 66:6 names the voice, "the voice of the LORD, repaying His enemies what they deserve". Revelation 16:1 does not name the speaker; the voice sends "the seven angels" with "the seven bowls of God's wrath", and in 16:17 says "It is done!" In 14:15 it is "another angel" who comes out of the temple and cries out.

rows.title: The courts of the LORD

The Law & history: the one who will build My house and My courts
the courts of the house of the LORD
in the courts of the house of God
a room in the courts of the house of God
Psalms & wisdom: Blessed is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts
My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD
better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere
they will flourish in the courts of our God
bring an offering and enter His courts
Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise
in the courts of the LORD's house
in the courts of the house of our God
The Prophets: will also have charge of My courts

rows.alike: The house has its courts: "the courts of the LORD" (Psalm 84:2), "the courts of the house of the LORD" (1 Chronicles 28:12), "My house and My courts" (1 Chronicles 28:6), "My courts" (Isaiah 1:12; Zechariah 3:7).
rows.different: The Psalms long for them and enter them: "better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere" (84:10). Isaiah 1:12 asks "who has required this of you"; in Zechariah 3:7 charge of the courts is promised on a condition, "If you walk in My ways"; in 1 Chronicles 28:6 it is the LORD's word that Solomon will build them; Nehemiah 13:7 tells of "the evil that Eliashib had done" there.

rows.title: Who may dwell in Your tent? To dwell in the house of the LORD

Psalms & wisdom: O LORD, who may abide in Your tent? Who may dwell on Your holy mountain?
He who walks with integrity and practices righteousness
I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever
Who may ascend the hill of the LORD? Who may stand in His holy place?
He who has clean hands and a pure heart
to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life
Let me dwell in Your tent forever
How blessed are those who dwell in Your house
the upright will dwell in Your presence
The Prophets: Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire? Who of us can dwell with everlasting flames?
He who walks righteously and speaks with sincerity

rows.alike: The question is asked and answered in the same form: "Who may dwell on Your holy mountain?" with "He who walks with integrity" (Psalm 15:1-2), "Who may ascend the hill of the LORD?" with "He who has clean hands and a pure heart" (Psalm 24:3-4), and "Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire?" with "He who walks righteously" (Isaiah 33:14-15).
rows.different: In Isaiah 33:14 the question is the cry of "The sinners in Zion", and the dwelling is "with a consuming fire". In Psalm 23:6 the speaker says "I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever"; in 27:4 he asks "to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life"; in 61:4, "Let me dwell in Your tent forever"; and Psalm 84:4 calls blessed "those who dwell in Your house".

rows.title: The LORD who dwells in Zion

The Law & history: has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever
Psalms & wisdom: Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion
This is the mountain God chose for His dwelling, where the LORD will surely dwell forever
His tent is in Salem, His dwelling place in Zion
For the LORD has chosen Zion; He has desired it for His home
here I will dwell, for I have desired this home
The Prophets: the LORD of Hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion
I am the LORD your God, who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain
For the LORD dwells in Zion
I will return to Zion and dwell in Jerusalem

rows.alike: The words "who dwells in Zion" are said in Psalm 9:11 and Joel 3:17, "who dwells on Mount Zion" in Isaiah 8:18, "dwell in Jerusalem" in 1 Chronicles 23:25 and Zechariah 8:3, and "dwells in Jerusalem" in Psalm 135:21.
rows.different: Psalm 132:14 gives the LORD's own word, "here I will dwell, for I have desired this home"; Zechariah 8:3 speaks of a return, "I will return to Zion"; Joel 3:17 adds "Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners"; in 1 Chronicles 23:25 it is David's word, with "has given rest to His people".

rows.title: Arise, O LORD, to Your resting place

The Law & history: the ark of the covenant of the LORD traveling ahead of them for those three days to seek a resting place for them
Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered
to build a house as a resting place for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and as a footstool for our God
arise, O LORD God, and enter Your resting place, You and the ark of Your might
Psalms & wisdom: God arises. His enemies are scattered
Arise, O LORD, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength
This is My resting place forever and ever
The Prophets: cut your resting place in the rock

rows.alike: The ark and the call to arise go together: "Rise up, O LORD!" when the ark set out (Numbers 10:35), "Arise, O LORD, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength" (Psalm 132:8), and "arise, O LORD God, and enter Your resting place, You and the ark of Your might" (2 Chronicles 6:41).
rows.different: In Numbers 10:33 the ark goes "to seek a resting place for them", and the cry is "May Your enemies be scattered", as in Psalm 68:1, "His enemies are scattered". In 1 Chronicles 28:2 it is "to build a house as a resting place for the ark"; Psalm 132:14 has "This is My resting place forever and ever". Isaiah 22:16 has "cut your resting place in the rock", beside "a tomb".

rows.title: Let us go up to the house of the LORD

Psalms & wisdom: Let us go to the house of the LORD
Let us go to His dwelling place; let us worship at His footstool
The Prophets: the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established as the chief of the mountains
Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob
the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established as the chief of the mountains
Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob
Arise, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God
Let us go at once to plead before the LORD and to seek the LORD of Hosts

rows.alike: "Let us go to the house of the LORD" (Psalm 122:1) and "let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob" (Isaiah 2:3; Micah 4:2); "let us go up to Zion" (Jeremiah 31:6).
rows.different: In Psalm 122:1 the speaker was "glad when they said to me". In Isaiah 2:2-3 and Micah 4:1-2, which run almost word for word alike, it is "In the last days", and the ones who say "Come, let us go up" are "many peoples" in Isaiah and "many nations" in Micah; in Jeremiah 31:6 "watchmen will call out on the hills of Ephraim"; in Zechariah 8:21 "the residents of one city will go to another".

rows.title: Take off your sandals: the place is holy

The Law & history: Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground
Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy
Gospels & Acts: Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground

rows.alike: All three have "Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy".
rows.different: Exodus 3:5 begins "Do not come any closer," God said, and ends "holy ground"; in Acts 7:33 "the Lord said to him". In Joshua 5:15 the speaker is "The Commander of the LORD's army", and "ground" is not said.

rows.title: Between the holy and the common

The Law & history: You must distinguish between the holy and the common, between the clean and the unclean
The Prophets: They make no distinction between the holy and the common
to separate the holy from the common
teach My people the difference between the holy and the common

rows.alike: The words "between the holy and the common" stand in Leviticus 10:10 and Ezekiel 22:26 and 44:23, each beside "between the clean and the unclean"; Ezekiel 42:20 has "to separate the holy from the common".
rows.different: Leviticus 10:10 is a command, "You must distinguish". Ezekiel 22:26 charges that "Her priests" "make no distinction"; Ezekiel 44:23 says "They are to teach My people the difference between the holy and the common"; in Ezekiel 42:20 a wall is "to separate the holy from the common".

rows.title: The veil

The Law & history: Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it
the veil will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place
screen off the ark with the veil
not to enter freely into the Most Holy Place behind the veil
bring its blood behind the veil
He made the veil of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim woven into it
Gospels & Acts: the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom
the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom
the veil of the temple was torn down the middle
The letters: Hebrews 6:19
It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain
Hebrews 9:3
Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place
Hebrews 10:20
by the new and living way opened for us through the curtain of His body

rows.alike: The veil stands before the Most Holy Place: "the veil will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place" (Exodus 26:33), "Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place" (Hebrews 9:3); Matthew, Mark and Luke each say "the veil of the temple was torn".
rows.different: In the Law the veil is made, "with cherubim skillfully worked into it", and Aaron is told "not to enter freely into the Most Holy Place behind the veil" (Leviticus 16:2). Matthew and Mark have "torn in two from top to bottom", Luke "torn down the middle". Hebrews uses "curtain": of hope, which "enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain" (6:19), and of "the new and living way opened for us through the curtain of His body" (10:20).

rows.title: The pattern shown you on the mountain

The Law & history: design all its furnishings according to the pattern I show you
See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain
set up the tabernacle according to the pattern shown you on the mountain
It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain
fashioned according to the pattern the LORD had shown Moses
David gave his son Solomon the plans for the portico of the temple
all the details of this plan, the LORD has made clear to me in writing by His hand upon me
Gospels & Acts: It was constructed exactly as God had directed Moses, according to the pattern he had seen
The letters: Hebrews 8:5
See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain

rows.alike: "See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain" stands word for word in Exodus 25:40 and Hebrews 8:5; Acts 7:44 has "according to the pattern he had seen".
rows.different: In Exodus 25:9 the words are "the pattern I show you", and Numbers 8:4 has "the pattern the LORD had shown Moses". Acts 7:44 says the tabernacle "was constructed exactly as God had directed Moses". Hebrews 8:5 has "The place where they serve is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven" and "Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle". In 1 Chronicles 28 "David gave his son Solomon the plans", and says "the LORD has made clear to me in writing".

rows.title: The tabernacle of the Testimony

The Law & history: the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the Testimony
appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the Testimony
the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the Testimony and watch over it
the tabernacle, the Tent of the Testimony, was set up
the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle of the Testimony
Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony
Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony
before the Tent of the Testimony
for the Tent of the Testimony
Gospels & Acts: Our fathers had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them in the wilderness
Revelation: the temple-the tabernacle of the Testimony-was opened in heaven

rows.alike: The name "the tabernacle of the Testimony" stands in Exodus 38:21, Numbers 1:50, 1:53 and 10:11, Acts 7:44 and Revelation 15:5, and "the Tent of the Testimony" in Numbers 9:15, 17:7, 17:8 and 18:2 and 2 Chronicles 24:6.
rows.different: In Numbers 1:53 the Levites "are to camp around the tabernacle of the Testimony and watch over it"; in 9:15 "the cloud covered it", and in 10:11 "the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle of the Testimony". In 17:7-8 "Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony". Acts 7:44 has "Our fathers had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them in the wilderness". Revelation 15:5 has "the temple-the tabernacle of the Testimony-was opened in heaven".

rows.title: Where I will meet with you

The Law & history: I will meet with you there above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim
where I will meet you to speak with you
I will also meet with the Israelites there, and that place will be consecrated by My glory
before the mercy seat that is over the Testimony-where I will meet with you
in front of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you
he heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the mercy seat
in front of the Testimony, where I meet with you
Psalms & wisdom: Your foes have roared within Your meeting place
They burned down every place where God met us in the land
The Prophets: He has destroyed His place of meeting

rows.alike: Exodus 30:6 and 30:36 have "where I will meet with you" of the place before the Testimony, and Numbers 17:4 "where I meet with you"; Psalm 74:4 has "Your meeting place" and Lamentations 2:6 "His place of meeting".
rows.different: In the Law the words are "I will speak with you" (Exodus 25:22) and "consecrated by My glory" (29:43), and Numbers 7:89 tells that Moses "heard the voice speaking to him". Psalm 74:8 says "They burned down every place where God met us in the land"; Lamentations 2:6 has "He has destroyed His place of meeting" and "laid waste His tabernacle like a garden booth".

rows.title: Seek His face

The Law & history: humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways
Psalms & wisdom: who seek Your face, O God of Jacob
Your face, O LORD, I will seek
I have sought Your face with all my heart
The Prophets: I will return to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face

rows.alike: The words "seek His face always" are word for word in 1 Chronicles 16:11 and Psalm 105:4; "seek My face" is the LORD's word in 2 Chronicles 7:14 and Hosea 5:15.
rows.different: In 2 Chronicles 7:14 seeking My face comes with "humble themselves and pray" and "I will hear from heaven"; Hosea 5:15 has "I will return to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face". Psalm 27:8 and 119:58 are said by the one who seeks: "Your face, O LORD, I will seek"; "I have sought Your face with all my heart". Psalm 24:6 has "the generation of those who seek Him", and 1 Chronicles 16:11 and Psalm 105:4 are a call: "Seek out the LORD and His strength; seek His face always".

rows.title: Joy in Your presence

Psalms & wisdom: You will fill me with joy in Your presence
You cheer him with joy in Your presence
Gospels & Acts: You will fill me with joy in Your presence

rows.alike: "You will fill me with joy in Your presence" stands word for word in Psalm 16:11 and Acts 2:28; Psalm 21:6 has "You cheer him with joy in Your presence".
rows.different: Psalm 16:11 has "the path of life" and Acts 2:28 "the paths of life"; the psalm goes on "with eternal pleasures at Your right hand", which Acts 2:28 does not include. Psalm 21:6 has "You cheer him with joy in Your presence", after "For You grant him blessings forever".

rows.title: From the presence of the LORD

The Law & history: they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God
Cain went out from the presence of the LORD
Fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed the burnt offering
fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed them
far from the presence of the LORD
Psalms & wisdom: Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD
So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD
Where can I flee from Your presence
The Prophets: to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD
he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD

rows.alike: The same words, "from the presence of the LORD", are used of hiding (Genesis 3:8), of going out (Genesis 4:16; Job 1:12), and of fleeing (Jonah 1:3), and Psalm 139:7 asks "Where can I flee from Your presence".
rows.different: Genesis 3:8 and Jonah tell of hiding and fleeing; Psalm 139:7 asks it as a question, beside "Where can I go to escape Your Spirit?" In Job it is "Satan" who goes out; in Leviticus 9:24 and 10:2 it is fire that "came out from the presence of the LORD", once consuming "the burnt offering" and once "consumed them".

rows.title: The whole earth filled with His glory

The Law & history: the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD
Psalms & wisdom: may all the earth be filled with His glory
The Prophets: all the earth is full of His glory
the earth shone with His glory
the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea
Revelation: the earth was illuminated by his glory

rows.alike: The earth is said to be filled with His glory: "the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD" (Numbers 14:21), "may all the earth be filled with His glory" (Psalm 72:19), "all the earth is full of His glory" (Isaiah 6:3).
rows.different: Numbers 14:21 has it with "as surely as I live"; Psalm 72:19 has "may all the earth be filled with His glory" after "blessed be His glorious name forever"; in Isaiah 6:3 it is what "they were calling out to one another". Habakkuk 2:14 adds "the knowledge of" and "as the waters cover the sea"; Ezekiel 43:2 has "I saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east" and "the earth shone with His glory".

rows.title: The house of God, the gate of heaven: angels going up and down

The Law & history: God's angels were going up and down the ladder
Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it
This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven
Gospels & Acts: you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man

rows.alike: In Jacob's dream "God's angels were going up and down the ladder" (Genesis 28:12); in John 1:51 He declares "you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man".
rows.different: In Genesis the angels go up and down a ladder "with its top reaching up to heaven", and Jacob says "This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven". In John 1:51 they ascend and descend "on the Son of Man", in a saying that begins "Truly, truly, I tell you" and says "you will all see heaven open".
